children.text: Participants
ThinkByte: Mukul M, Harsha Thota, Samarpith Rout, Charan Kumar, Pavan Kalyan, Revanth Babu Raavi, Vamsi Rampalli
Sigmainfo: Magesh R, Sonam Dahake, Sandeep Phophaliya, to: Shiresha Madhury, Divya Mishra, Neeraj Gupta
Key Takeaways

A detailed SEO strategy for the Australian and New Zealand markets was confirmed, emphasizing a subfolder approach to leverage the main domain’s authority with fully localized e-commerce landing pages.

Metrics reporting was updated with last week’s figures revealing 511 total users, 471 new users, 89 decisions, and a Jan-first query breakdown showing 32 inquiries with two legitimate e-commerce leads.
It was decided to integrate query fan out pages into the content strategy, ensuring page structures include local language elements and specific query answers to strengthen search presence.
Discussions confirmed that the current lead form (powered by Contact Form 7) includes validation measures, but further refinement is needed to prequalify leads and reduce junk submissions.
Attention was drawn to consolidating Google Business Profiles, with plans to properly set up and optimize profiles for the US and Australian locations to avoid confusion and boost local SEO.
Action Items
Harsha Thota
Consolidate the existing Google Business Profile listings for Sigma Info Solutions across all locations by obtaining necessary access and cleaning/updating the content to optimize for local keywords.

Adapt the current Shopify ecommerce landing page's query fan notes into a localized Australian version within a subfolder, ensuring usage of Australian English, local addresses, currencies, and region-specific content.
Revanth Babu Raavi
Set up (or re-establish) the USA Google Business Profile for Sigma Info Solutions to ensure correct presence in relevant searches.
Share the URL structure samples for Sigma Info Solutions post-meeting.
Evaluate and compare language tag configuration options (e.g. using language plus country codes) for localized URLs and decide on the optimal setup.
to: Shiresha Madhury
Provide a weekly breakup report of lead inquiries detailing valid leads versus job seeker queries, with metrics showing conversion trends.
Detail and share the technical and process requirements for LLMs and Bing integration so that team members (e.g., Mahesh) can assist accordingly.
Magesh R
Share the available server logs (covering the last 30 days) and, if possible, plan for a process to retain and share logs for a 90-day period in future monthly reports.
Objective

Plan of action for the Australian and New Zealand markets to tap ecommerce, involving keyword research, content brief creation, and a subfolder strategy to leverage main domain authority; strategy documented and in progress.
Target Audience
Focus on local businesses and users in Australia and New Zealand seeking ecommerce, BI analytics, and fintech solutions, with content tailored using localized language and market-specific examples.
Messaging & Positioning

Position the subfolder approach as a way to harness existing domain authority, delivering localized content with schema implementation, query fanout pages, and answer-box optimization to capture high intent search queries.
Channels

Utilize organic Google search with localized landing pages, Google Business Profiles, website chat buttons, backlink directories, and case studies; track UTM parameters to monitor leads from sources like Charge GPT.
Timeline
Meeting held on 2026-01-21T14:00:00+05:30; URL structure samples to be shared post-call and monthly server log reports to be provided starting from the next month.
Budget
Metrics

Reported metrics include 511 total users, 471 new users, and 89 decisions last week; from January 1, 32 inquiries received with only 2 legitimate ecommerce queries, with plans for a weekly lead breakup analysis.
Creative Requirements

Content should be highly localized with region-specific language (Australian English), addresses, local currency, and imagery; new query fanout pages and appropriate AHref Lang meta tags are required.
Dependencies

Depends on consolidating access to multiple Google Business Profiles across regions (India, USA, Australia) and obtaining updated URL structure details from the product team; monthly server log extracts are needed from Magesh R.
Risk
Risks include receiving junk leads from job seekers or bots, potential CTR drops due to evolving Google query fanout layouts, and inconsistent GBP profiles across regions affecting search visibility.
SEO Implementation Plan
Plan to perform keyword research for Australian and New Zealand e-commerce markets.
Adopt subfolder strategy to leverage main domain authority rather than fresh domains.
Utilize language and region-specific meta tags to ensure proper geographical targeting.
Implement localized content with local addresses, currencies, reviews, and region-specific examples.
AI Services Expansion
Decision to add AI/ML services following the establishment of e-commerce and BI pages.
Expansion into AI and fintech services planned incrementally as main pages are optimized.
Performance Tracking
Metrics tracked include 511 total users, 471 new users, and 89 decisions.
Plan to implement a weekly breakdown of lead types and conversion trends, along with sharing monthly server logs.
Lead Quality Assessment
32 inquiries received since Jan 1 with only 2 valid e-commerce leads; majority are job seekers.
Discussed improving prequalification filters to reduce junk leads through enhanced form validations.
Query Fanout Strategy
Google’s new search listing format introduces query fanout sections affecting visibility.
Plan to build multiple landing pages targeting specific query fanouts, such as Shopify migration services.
GBP Profile Management
Existing GBP profiles in Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Jodhpur; US profile missing and needs setup.
Ensure business name is correctly listed as 'Sigma Info Solutions' for profile optimization.
